feature: A walk names a panel row by something a rename cannot break
summary: Scripted walks used to find a row in Appearance or the Effects list by the words printed on it, so changing one word broke walks by the dozen: five repair tasks in one day, all from Outline becoming Border. Every one of those rows now carries a second name that comes off the model instead of the copy, and a walk can use it: in: "@border" keeps working the day the row starts saying something else.
setup: Nothing to turn on in the app. This is the scripted playtest harness, so it is read rather than clicked: Scripts/playtest/*.json and docs/design/playtest-harness.md.

try.do: Open docs/design/playtest-harness.md and read "A row of the panel has a second name that a rename cannot touch".
Open Scripts/playtest/effects-remembered-walk.json and read the steps: every Border, Shadow and Blur is now @border, @shadow, @blur.
Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/effects-remembered-walk.json and watch it pass.
Change EffectKind.border.title in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerEffects.swift from "Border" to "Outline".
Run the same walk again. It still passes, and the picture now says Outline where it said Border.
Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/border-offset-walk.json, which was left naming the row by its word. It fails.

evaluate: Reading a converted walk, can you still tell what it is doing, or does @border make it harder to follow than Border did?
Is the mark the right one? @border reads as a handle to me, but #border or border: were both on the table.
Twenty walks were converted and about three hundred were not. Should the rest be converted in one pass, or only as they are next touched?
A steady name says the row, never the control: press "Switch" in "@border". Does that split feel natural, or would you expect @border.switch?
A walk can now write reads: "off" instead of reads: "Border, off". Is the shorter claim still saying enough?
rough: The rows of an ordinary menu still go by their words. The one exception is the plus menu in Effects, where choose: "@border" works, because that menu is built straight off the same model the rows are. Everywhere else a menu row is read off a list rather than addressed, and giving every menu item in the app a durable id is a separate job.

Only the two lists whose words are product copy were given steady names: the parts in Appearance and the entries in the Effects list. Width, Height, Layout and Position & Size are structural words that have not moved in the whole history of the queue, and giving them ids would be noise for no cover.

Three of the twenty walks still fail, and they failed the same way before this change: border-effect, glow-effect and label-fills-a-row each stop on a control the dock has scrolled out of reach. Filed separately as "Three walks stop on a panel control the dock has scrolled out of reach" with the commands and output.
I did not run the whole 322-walk sweep, which is about 52 minutes and five times a runner's ceiling. I ran the twenty walks I changed plus two controls, and asked the loop for a sweep.
The screenshot is a real screen capture: the Grants line said the probe had Screen Recording.
